title: St. Louis: Tom Turpin, Jazzland and the district
summary: The interviewer asks about Turpin's Jazzland, the Booker T. Washington Theater and the St. Louis red-light district; St. Cyr recalls the layout but never heard Turpin play.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Yeah, every night sometimes. Yeah. Do you remember in St. Louis any of the places like Tom Turpin and his brother Charlie ran the place Jazzland?
Yeah, we used to go to the Jazzland.
But the theater they had was the Booker T. Washington?
Yeah, Booker T. Washington Theater was on the corner. And right behind it, on Market Street, was the Jazzland.
Like you said, the theater was on the corner here. And right this house here, back of it, would be the Jazzland. Yeah.

The filling station. I took pictures of where it used to be. There's one place, remember the Rose... Once it was called the Rosebud or Hunting and Shooting Club. It was down on Market Street, a little bit down towards the river.
The Turpin's had a saloon there where Tom used to play piano. Did you ever hear Tom Turpin play piano? No, I never heard him play, no.
He was the famous Ragnarok piano player. They tell me he was a very good piano.
Was the St. Louis District Red Light District over in Chessland, was it still running in those days in 1990?
No, no. They put the damp on Prohibition End. I mean, the damp went on while we went to St. Louis. And I used to go to the chauffeur's club very often.
Well, that was still running when I was in the 1930s and 40s. Yeah.
The other time the guy went broke. When the liquor came in, he put in liquor and he was making lots of money and he started playing fast women and slow horses and broke him.
